question: What is the full name of the University?
answer: COMSATS University Islamabad (CUI).

question: What is an abbreviation of COMSATS?
answer: Commission on Science and Technology for Sustainable Development in the South (COMSATS).

question: Is CUI a private or Public Sector University?
answer: It's a Federally Chartered, Public sector University.

question: Is University recognized by Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan?
answer: Yes, University is recognized by the Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan.

question: How many campuses does university have?
answer: There are seven campuses of CUI: Islamabad campus, Lahore campus, Abbottabad Campus, Sahiwal Campus, Vehari Campus, Wah Campus, Attock Campus.

question: What is system of education being followed at CUI?
answer: CUI follows semester system. There are two semesters in a year i.e. Spring (February – June) and Fall (September – January).

question: Is there any age limit for applying for admission in Undergraduate degree programs?
answer: There is no age limit. CUI provides equal opportunity to all the applicant purely on merit bases.

question: How Frequently Admissions are offered at CUI?
answer: CUI offers admissions in Undergraduate and Graduate degree programs twice in a year i.e. Fall and Spring session.

question: Does Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC) recognize engineering programs of CUI?
answer: Yes, all the engineering programs offered by CUI are recognized by Pakistan Engineering Council.

question: Does COMSATS University have highly qualified faculty in various disciplines?
answer: Yes, COMSATS has highly qualified and experienced faculty in various disciplines in accordance with the guidelines provided by HEC.

question: Does NCEAC and NBEAC recognize computer science and Management Science programs of CUI?
answer: Yes, all degree programs at all campuses of CUI are recognized by HEC and their relevant accreditation bodies.

question: Does COMSATS University have lab facilities?
answer: Yes, COMSATS has latest and well-equipped relevant laboratories to support programs being offered at Undergraduate and Graduate level.

question: Does COMSATS have computer lab facilities?
answer: Yes, COMSATS has modern classrooms and well-equipped updated computer labs as well as high speed internet facility.

question: Does COMSATS have library facility?
answer: Yes, all the campuses of COMSATS have state-of-the-art modern library facilities, having access to specialized digital resources and databases. Sufficient subject-wise books and journals are also available.

question: Do applicants with DAE qualification qualify to apply for admission in Engineering Programs?
answer: Yes, on open merit for DAE applicants who can apply for the Engineering Programs in line with the policy guidelines provided by the Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC).

question: Is there any self-finance / quota system in COMSATS?
answer: No, admissions are offered on open merit basis.

question: Does COMSATS provide Hostel Facility?
answer: Mostly all the campuses have hostel facility/hostel facilitation center, but it is better to contact the respective Admission Office of that campus for further confirmation.

question: Does COMSATS provide a transport Facility for the students?
answer: Yes, CUI provides transport facility to their students.

question: When do the classes commence?
answer: Fall semester commences in the 1st week of September, whereas the Spring semester commences in the 1st week of February.

question: Does CUI entertain transfer/migration cases?
answer: CUI does not have a credit hours transfer policy from any National or International Institute/university. However, a student of CUI can transfer his/her credit hours to other universities either national or international.

question: What is the duration of undergraduate and graduate (MS/Ph.D) degree programs?
answer: Bachelor programs: 4 Years (minimum 8 semesters, maximum 12). MS programs: 2 Years (minimum 4 semesters, maximum 8). PhD programs: 3 Years (minimum 6 semesters, maximum 14).

question: What is the medium of instruction in CUI?
answer: English is the medium of instruction in CUI.

question: If my name on CNIC / Passport is different from the one mentioned on my academic documents, how can I get the same name on my degree/transcript issued by CUI?
answer: At the time of admission, the applicant is required to enter his/her personal data (name, father name, Date of Birth (DOB)) in accordance with his/her Secondary School Certificate (SSC) / O-Levels certificate. However, in case of any change in student name, you will first be required to get the SSC/O-Level DMC/Certificate revised and submit the revised SSC/O-Level certificate to CUI for change in name. Please note that you need to apply for the change in name, father name, or DOB well before the printing of the final transcript. In case of applying after printing of transcript/Degree, you will be required to pay the prescribed fee.

question: Is there any part time degree programs or short course(s)/diploma offered by CUI?
answer: CUI offers full time degree programs.

question: Does CUI Islamabad Campus offer any weekend programs?
answer: Currently, no weekend programs are being offered by CUI.

question: How can an applicant apply for admission in Comsats?
answer: One can apply for admission online through the website www.admissions.comsats.edu.pk

question: If I am filling the admission form and my online admission portal is stuck due to any reason, what should I do?
answer: In case the admission page is not loading properly, the applicant is advised to change/update the web browser (e.g. Google Chrome, Opera etc.); if the problem still exists then contact the admission office via e-mail and through the message center.

question: Can I apply for admission in multiple campuses?
answer: Yes, a candidate can apply for admission to more than one campus by filling up a new admission form, making a new login, and using a different e-mail address than used previously, then completing all the campus formalities of that campus.

question: Will there be any deduction of marks at undergraduate level if my FA/FSc/A-Level is not fresh?
answer: There will be no deduction of marks in any case from overall merit.

question: What are the eligibility criteria for admission in different undergraduate programs?
answer: To see eligibility criteria, visit the website (http://admissions.comsats.edu.pk/Home/EligibilityCriteria?pt=BS)

question: Is it mandatory to deposit admission processing fee?
answer: Yes, it is mandatory for the student to deposit the application processing fee through a challan form at any online bank branch mentioned on the voucher.

question: Is application processing fee refundable?
answer: Processing fee will not be refunded.

question: Is admission processing fee for one campus acceptable for all other campuses?
answer: No, the candidate must submit the admission processing fee for each campus separately through a challan form available on the admission portal.

question: Is it necessary to send the hard copy of the processing fee paid challan form to the Admission Office of the campus?
answer: There is no need to send the hard copy to the Admission Office, but it is mandatory for each applicant to upload the image of their paid challan while filling up the application on the online admission portal.

question: Can I select more than one choice on the admission form?
answer: Yes, you can select more than one choice on the admission form of the same degree level.

question: Can I edit information in my admission application?
answer: Yes, you can edit your online admission form before submission. Once your admission form is received by the admission office, the candidate cannot edit any information on the admission form.

question: How can I edit my information on a submitted admission form?
answer: To edit your information on an already submitted admission form, you will contact the admission office and submit an editing request either via e-mail or through the message center available in the online admission portal.

question: Does CUI allow result-awaiting candidates to apply for admission at Undergraduate level?
answer: Yes, COMSATS allows result-awaiting applicants of F.Sc (Part-2) to apply for admission on the basis of their F.Sc Part-1 result having no 'F' grade in each course. However, the merit of the A-Level (A2) result-awaiting student will be determined based on the Matric/O-level submitted equivalence certificate (issued by IBCC) at the time of admission.

question: What will be the status of my admission in case of result awaiting?
answer: You will be offered provisional/conditional admission which will be confirmed after submission and verification of your SSC/O-Level and HSSC/A-level Certificate.

question: My percentage in F.A/F.Sc part-1 is less than 60% (for Engineering and Architecture) or 50% (for non-engineering programs). Can I apply for admission?
answer: In any case, your provisional admission will be cancelled with immediate effect if you fail to achieve minimum 60% marks in HSSC for Engineering and Architecture programs and minimum 50% marks for Non-engineering programs.

question: Can I apply for admission in CUI having a Supply in FA/F.Sc part-1 Exam?
answer: A student having a supply in FA/F.Sc part-1 cannot apply for admission. However, they can apply for admission in the next session with a complete FA/F.Sc pass result.

question: A student who has given improvement exams (FA/F.Sc) and is waiting for the final result — can he/she apply for admission?
answer: They can only apply for admission on the basis of their old/available FA/F.Sc complete results, subject to meeting the eligibility criteria of a program. However, they can update their FA/F.Sc improved result by contacting the Admission Office once the result is announced by their respective board, before the merit list is published. After the display of the merit list, improved F.Sc results will not be considered.

question: Can a Pre-medical student with Additional Maths (result awaiting) apply for Engineering programs?
answer: Yes, they can apply for admission on the basis of the F.Sc part-1 exam. However, they will be treated as a result-awaiting candidate and, while filling up the admission form, must mention their F.Sc part-1 result and furnish an Affidavit on stamp paper that he/she appeared for the Additional Maths exam prior to applying for admission in CUI.

question: I have completed my FA/F.Sc. Can I mention overall complete FA/F.Sc result?
answer: Students who have completed their FA/F.Sc/A-Levels are required to mention overall FA/F.Sc result.

question: Is it mandatory for an applicant who has completed O-level and A-level to obtain equivalence from IBCC while applying for admission in CUI?
answer: Yes, the applicant must obtain the equivalence of O-Level and A-level from the Inter Board Chairman Committee (IBCC) before applying for admission in CUI.

question: How will an A-Level result-awaiting student apply for admission in CUI?
answer: An A-Level result-awaiting student can apply for admission on the basis of his/her Matric/O-Level exam equivalence certificate issued by IBCC.

question: How will the merit of an A-Level result-awaiting applicant be calculated?
answer: The merit of an A-level result-awaiting applicant will be formulated based upon the Matric/O-Level Equivalency plus Entry exam. In case of any restriction beyond human control, where the entry exam is not possible to be conducted, the directive of the Government of Pakistan will be followed.

question: Is it mandatory for the A-Level student to produce A-Level equivalency while applying for admission in CUI?
answer: If the candidate has already cleared/completed A-Level, then he/she must submit an A-Level equivalence certificate from IBCC at CUI. Moreover, if a student is unable to produce A-Level equivalency, then merit will NOT be formulated based upon grade letter.

question: What if an A-Level result-awaiting student is unable to produce O-Level equivalency while applying for admission in CUI?
answer: If the student is unable to produce O-Level equivalency, then the form will be rejected.

question: Can O&A Level students obtain combined equivalency of O&A Level from IBCC?
answer: Students of O&A Level will request IBCC to issue O-level (10th grade) and A-level (12th grade) equivalency separately, as it is a requirement of the university for merit calculation.

question: How will a candidate from American/GED/foreign board apply for admission?
answer: A student who applies for admission from American/GED/foreign board will get the equivalency of 10th and 12th grade separately from IBCC. If he/she is unable to produce equivalency documents, the admission form will be rejected.

question: Does CUI arrange any entry exam for the candidate?
answer: Yes, CUI conducts an entry exam at the time of admissions for Undergraduate and Graduate program applicants.

question: What is the difference between NAT and GAT, and for which exam will I register myself?
answer: NAT stands for National Aptitude Test. Candidates who apply for admission at bachelor level will appear in the NAT test. GAT General stands for Graduate Aptitude Test. Candidates who apply for admission in an MS program will appear in the GAT General test. GAT Subject stands for Graduate Aptitude Test. Candidates who apply for admission in Ph.D programs will appear in the GAT Subject test.

question: What are the passing marks in the entry exam?
answer: For Bachelor Level: applicant is advised to get maximum marks in the test to be able to qualify for merit. For MS Level: 50 score is the passing score in the GAT General test. For Ph.D Level: 60 score is the passing score in the GAT Subject test.

question: I have not passed/appeared in any NAT/GAT test scheduled by the NTS. Can I still apply for admission?
answer: Yes, you can register yourself for the NAT/GAT test arranged by CUI exclusively for CUI applicants.

question: In which NAT test category will I appear for the test?
answer: The NAT test category is based upon what you have studied in your FA/F.Sc/A-Levels; you will select and appear in the test category that is relevant to your FA/F.Sc/A-Levels group of study. For example, if you are a pre-medical student, you will appear in the IM exam of the NAT test — even if you are applying to BBA or A&F program. The test is based upon what you have studied in the past.

question: Is the NTS test fee included in the processing fee?
answer: The NTS test fee is not included in the processing fee of CUI admissions. To register for the entry test through COMSATS, the applicant will pay a separate NTS registration fee.

question: If I have passed the NTS exam before, will it be enough for admission?
answer: If you had a valid (in terms of expiry date) NAT/GAT test result at the time of submitting the admission application, it will be accepted for admission processing and merit calculation. However, each semester CUI receives a huge number of applications for various programs, and in some programs the number of seats is limited. To qualify on merit, it is advised to re-appear for the NTS test to improve your test score for merit competition.

question: If I have a valid NAT/GAT test result and I have also appeared in CUI's NTS test, which result will be considered for the merit?
answer: If you have submitted a previous valid score card with your admission application and register yourself for another NAT/GAT test, the best score from both results will be counted for the merit calculation.

question: If I am applying for admission in more than one campus, will I have to appear for the test from each campus?
answer: One campus's NTS test is applicable for other campus(es); there is no need to re-register yourself for the NTS test from multiple campuses. However, the following points must be kept in mind: 1. The admission closing date of CUI campuses can be different. 2. The student will fill up the admission form and register for the NAT/GAT test of the campus whose closing date is earlier. 3. Later, fill up the admission form of any other campus. 4. While filling up the admission form of the 2nd campus, he/she can mention their CUI roll no (which is their form number) in the NTS section.

question: Where should I send the paid voucher of NTS?
answer: The candidate is advised to keep the hard copy of the paid NTS challan. However, it is mandatory for each applicant to upload the image of their paid challan while filling up the application on the online admission portal.

question: Does COMSATS accept other university's NTS (NAT/GAT) test?
answer: COMSATS does not accept the entry test/NTS test score of any other institute/university. However, CUI will accept the score of candidates who appeared for the NAT/GAT test through NTS.

question: If I have appeared for the NAT/GAT test through NTS and do not have an original test card, what should I do?
answer: You can furnish the internet-generated result from the NTS website for admission.

question: Can I use CUI's NTS test result for other university admissions?
answer: It is purely at the discretion of that university/institute to accept CUI's NAT/GAT result.

question: From where can I get the preparation material for the NTS exam?
answer: You can purchase the NTS book for preparation from any book shop.

question: Can I get admission in an MS/Ph.D program without appearing in the GAT test at the time of admission?
answer: It is mandatory for each candidate to appear and pass the GAT test at the time of admission. Admission will not be granted without the GAT exam. For MS candidates, GAT General is mandatory, whereas for Ph.D, GAT Subject is mandatory.

question: If I have passed the GAT-General exam, should that be enough to secure admission in CUI?
answer: GAT-General/GAT exams are the pre-requisite of the admission process for MS/Ph.D candidates. A candidate will only get a call for the departmental test/interview upon qualifying their respective GAT exam. After passing the departmental test/interview, the candidate's name will be recommended for merit, and the university will offer admission accordingly. Candidates unqualified in the interview will not get an offer of admission.

question: In case my NAT/GAT score expires before the closing date, will it be considered for admissions?
answer: If an applicant's NAT/GAT test score expires before the closing date of the admission application, the candidate will need to register and appear for the test again through CUI, otherwise the admission form will not be considered.

question: Does work experience count in the calculation of my aggregate merit for admission in the MS program?
answer: Work experience is not considered in the merit list calculation for admission in the MS program.

question: Can a result-awaiting candidate apply for MS/Ph.D admission?
answer: I couldn't find this information in the knowledge base. (Note: The answer text for Question No. 68 was not legibly captured in the source documents).

question: There is a 3rd division in my academic career; can I apply for the MS/Ph.D program?
answer: There shall not be a 3rd Division throughout academic career for applying to the MS/Ph.D program.

question: What is the university's refund policy?
answer: In case of cancellation/withdrawal of admission at CUI, refund will be made as per policy: 100% refund up to 10th day of classes; 50% refund from 11th to 15th day of classes; 0% refund after the 15th day of classes. Admission fee, registration fee, and Endowment Fund are non-refundable. Timeline covers both weekdays and weekends.

question: In case I am unable to meet the eligibility criteria of a program, what is CUI's policy?
answer: In case you are unable to meet the eligibility criteria of a program after declaration of board result, your admission will be cancelled immediately, and all your deposited dues will be refunded upon submission of the failed result transcript/DMC.

question: How much time does the university take for refund of dues?
answer: New admission refund-of-dues cases are initiated in the 1st week of commencement of classes and take two (02) weeks.

question: Does the university provide installments at the time of admission?
answer: CUI Islamabad Campus does not provide installments at the time of admission; however, this option is available at some of the CUI campuses.

question: Does the fee structure of CUI remain the same/constant throughout my degree program?
answer: No, it will change as and when notified by the university from time to time.

question: What is the procedure to cancel a new admission?
answer: If a candidate wants to cancel the admission, he/she will submit a written application duly signed by the parents and the candidate, along with: 1. Photocopy of Offer letter. 2. Photocopy of paid fee challan. You must apply within the timeline specified in the refund policy.

question: Is it possible to apply after the deadline? What is the late application policy?
answer: Applications cannot be submitted after the deadline. There is no late application/fee policy.

question: May I appeal against the admission decision and ask the admission office to explain in writing?
answer: Each semester CUI receives a large volume of applications and has a limited number of seats. The decision regarding admission is final. Due to the high volume, it is not possible to provide written feedback to each unsuccessful applicant.

question: If I have been admitted, can I defer my current semester?
answer: Attending the first semester at CUI is compulsory, and deferment is not an option for Undergraduate applicants. However, an applicant of a graduate program may defer his/her first semester in case of special circumstances such as a medical issue, etc.

question: I was selected in a previous admission cycle and did not join. Can I avail the previous admission offer in the current admission cycle?
answer: The previous admission offer was valid only for that previous semester and was time-limited.

question: How can I check my application status?
answer: You can check your application status by logging into your online admission portal. When your application is processed, this message will appear on screen: 'Your application is successfully verified'.

question: Can I change my program after depositing the dues?
answer: Yes, a student can change his/her program before commencement of classes, subject to fulfillment of the following requirements: 1. Meeting the pre-requisite/eligibility criteria of the program. 2. Meeting the closing merit of the said program. 3. Availability of a seat.

question: How can I change my program after commencement of classes?
answer: After commencement of classes, you must submit a written application to the concerned HoD, who will forward it to the Department of Academics. Change of program requests are only entertained till the end of the first week of classes.

question: If I got admission in one campus and later another campus of CUI offers me admission in the same session, shall my admission be transferred?
answer: Yes. Paid dues will be transferred to the destination campus. You must submit a written application and produce the offer letter of the campus to which you intend to transfer. The transfer case will then be initiated by the Admission Office.

question: I have accepted the provisional admission offer by submitting the dues. Do I have to submit any documents to the university?
answer: Yes. Submit: 1. Printed Admission Form from portal. 2. Two passport-size photographs (one attested front, one back). 3. CNIC or B-Form copy. 4. SSC and Mark Sheet copy (or O-Level equivalence). 5. HSSC Certificate copy (or HSSC Part 1 result card / A-Level equivalence). 6. Valid NTS Result Card. 7. Affidavit for result-awaiting candidates (PKR 20 or 50). 8. Undertaking (PKR 20 or 50).

question: What mistake(s) must I avoid while applying to CUI for admission?
answer: Ensure: 1. You meet program eligibility. 2. Correct spellings of name and father's name as on official documents. 3. Clear/complete upload of result card images. 4. Clear image of paid processing/NTS challan. 5. Click 'Submit' after completing the form.

question: I completed and submitted my online admission application. Am I done now?
answer: Check your console regularly for: 'Your form has been Verified', 'Your form has been Verified and the Test has been Registered' (print your roll slip), or 'There is an objection on your admission application. Please address it before the deadline.'

question: There is an objection on my submitted admission application. What shall I do now?
answer: Read the objection carefully on the portal and resolve/address it before the form submission deadline; otherwise, your application will not be processed.

question: How shall I be informed about objection(s) on my submitted admission application?
answer: You will be informed (only before the deadline) via: 1. Portal dashboard message. 2. Registered email address.

question: How can I come to know that I have been selected in any program?
answer: You can view your merit status by logging into the admission portal. Selected candidates can download their offer letters and challans directly from there.

question: Does CUI have any merit calculator on their website?
answer: Yes, a merit calculator is available on the official admission website.

question: What is COMSATS University Islamabad (CUI)?
answer: COMSATS University Islamabad (CUI) is a public-sector university recognized by the Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan. CUI Wah Campus is one of its constituent campuses.

question: Is CUI Wah Campus recognized by HEC?
answer: Yes. CUI Wah Campus is a constituent campus of COMSATS University Islamabad, which is recognized by the Higher Education Commission (HEC).

question: Is CUI Wah Campus a public or private university?
answer: It is a public-sector university.

question: Where is CUI Wah Campus located?
answer: CUI Wah Campus is located in Wah Cantt, Punjab, Pakistan.

question: Which degree programs are offered?
answer: CUI Wah Campus offers BS, MS, and PhD programs in Computing, Engineering, Management Sciences, Mathematics, Psychology, and English (Linguistics).

question: What is the medium of instruction?
answer: English is the medium of instruction for all degree programs.

question: Is the semester system followed?
answer: Yes. All academic programs follow the semester system.

question: How many semesters are there in a BS degree?
answer: A BS degree consists of eight regular semesters.

question: How long does an MS degree take?
answer: Normally two years (four semesters).

question: How long does a PhD degree take?
answer: Normally three to five years, depending on research progress.

question: Which BS programs are offered at CUI Wah?
answer: BS Computer Science, BS Artificial Intelligence, BS Software Engineering (Non-Engineering), BS Computer Engineering, BS Electrical Engineering, BS Civil Engineering, BS Mechanical Engineering, BS Business Administration, BS Accounting & Finance, and BS Psychology.

question: What is the minimum percentage in Intermediate required for BS admission?
answer: Computing Programs: 50%. Engineering Programs: 60%. BBA, BAF & Psychology: 50%.

question: Can ICS/FCS students apply for Engineering?
answer: Yes. ICS students with Mathematics, Physics, and Computer Science and at least 60% marks are eligible for engineering programs.

question: Can Pre-Engineering students apply for Computer Science?
answer: Yes, Pre-Engineering students can apply for Computer Science.

question: Can Pre-Medical students apply for Computer Science?
answer: Yes, subject to the university's admission policy (studying/passing additional mathematics requirements).

question: Can Pre-Medical students apply for Artificial Intelligence?
answer: Yes, Pre-Medical students can apply for Artificial Intelligence.

question: Can Pre-Medical students apply for Software Engineering?
answer: Yes, Pre-Medical students are eligible to apply for Software Engineering.

question: Can I.Com students apply for BBA/BAF?
answer: Yes, I.Com students can apply for BBA (Business Administration) and BAF (Accounting & Finance).

question: Can FA/General Science students apply for BS Psychology/BBA/BAF?
answer: Yes, FA and General Science students can apply for BS Psychology, BBA, and BAF.

question: How much overall aggregate is required to qualify for merit?
answer: A minimum of 50% overall aggregate is required to qualify for the merit list.

question: What is the minimum percentage in ICS/F.Sc. (Pre-Engg) required for Engineering?
answer: A minimum of 60% marks in HSSC/ICS is required to apply for Engineering programs.

question: Can DAE students apply for Engineering?
answer: Yes, DAE students can apply if they possess a relevant DAE technology recognized for that specific engineering discipline.

question: Which DAE technologies are accepted for Engineering?
answer: Relevant technologies for Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, and Computer Engineering as approved by the competent authority and PEC.

question: Can A-Level students apply for admission?
answer: Yes, with an equivalence certificate issued by IBCC and fulfillment of program-specific eligibility requirements.

question: Is NAT compulsory for Undergraduate admission?
answer: Yes, NAT is compulsory for admission at the bachelor level.

question: What is the desired minimum NAT score to qualify for the merit list?
answer: A minimum score of 33% is required in the NAT test to qualify for merit list processing.

question: Which NAT is required for Computer Science?
answer: NAT-ICS is required for Computer Science programs.

question: Which NAT is required for Engineering?
answer: NAT-IE is required for Engineering programs.

question: Which NAT is required for Pre-Medical students?
answer: NAT-IM is required for Pre-Medical students.

question: Which NAT is required for I.Com students?
answer: NAT-ICom is required for I.Com students.

question: Which NAT is required for FA students?
answer: NAT-IA is required for FA students.

question: Which NAT is required for General Science students?
answer: NAT-IGS is required for General Science students.

question: Can I improve my NAT score?
answer: Yes. Applicants may appear in multiple NAT tests to improve their score in accordance with NTS guidelines.

question: Is a NAT test already passed by a candidate valid for admission?
answer: Yes, provided the test result is valid and has not expired before the closing date of the admission applications.

question: Which MS programs are offered at CUI Wah Campus?
answer: MS Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Artificial Intelligence Engineering, Cyber Security, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Mathematics, Management Sciences, Project Management, and English (Linguistics).

question: What is the minimum CGPA required for MS admission?
answer: A minimum of 2.50 CGPA (out of 4.00) or 55% marks in a relevant 16-year degree is required.

question: Can I apply for MS Project Management with an Engineering degree or any other degree?
answer: Yes. Any recognized 16-year degree holder is eligible to apply for MS Project Management.

question: Is HEC documents attestation required for MS students?
answer: Yes. The qualifying candidate needs to get their BS degree/Transcript attested by the HEC or equivalent authority.

question: Which PhD programs are offered at CUI Wah?
answer: Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Mathematics, and Management Sciences.

question: What CGPA is required for PhD admission?
answer: A minimum CGPA of 3.00 (out of 4.00) in the respective MS/MPhil program or 60% marks is required.

question: Is a thesis-based MS/MPhil required for PhD?
answer: Yes, a thesis-based MS/MPhil is required.

question: Can students with a non-thesis MS apply for PhD?
answer: No, students with a non-thesis MS/MPhil cannot apply.

question: Is HEC attestation required for PhD candidates?
answer: Yes. Both BS and MS/MPhil degrees and transcripts must be attested by HEC.

question: How do I apply for admission?
answer: Submit an online application through the official CUI admission portal.

question: Can I apply for more than one program?
answer: Yes, candidates can apply for multiple programs of the same degree level, according to the university's admission policy.

question: How is merit calculated?
answer: Merit is calculated according to the approved university admission policy based on academic records and entry test marks.

question: Does meeting eligibility guarantee admission?
answer: No. Admission is strictly competitive and merit-based due to a limited number of seats.

question: Can I change my program after admission?
answer: Requests to change programs are dealt with according to university regulations, subject to closing merit requirements and seat availability.

question: Can I freeze my semester?
answer: Yes. Students may apply for a semester freeze according to university regulations, but note that first-semester undergraduate students are not allowed to freeze/defer.

question: Can I resume my studies after freezing a semester?
answer: Yes, after completing the prescribed rejoining procedure within the allowed time frame.

question: What documents are required for application?
answer: Academic documents (Matric/FSc transcripts), CNIC/B-Form, photographs, NAT result (if applicable), paid challan image, and any specific forms required by the program.

question: When are merit lists displayed?
answer: Merit lists are displayed on the portal as per the official admission schedule announced by the university.

question: What happens if I miss the fee deposit deadline?
answer: The admission offer will be cancelled and the seat will be offered to the next candidate on the waiting list.

question: Is there any admission scholarship?
answer: No. There are no automatic admission scholarships based on entry scores.

question: Is there any merit scholarship?
answer: Yes. The Academic Excellence Scholarship is available for eligible BS students based on their semester results.

question: Are MS students eligible for scholarships?
answer: No, CUI does not offer merit scholarships to MS students.

question: Are PhD students eligible for scholarships?
answer: No.

question: When is the merit scholarship awarded?
answer: After evaluation of semester results according to university policy.

question: Is hostel facility available?
answer: Yes, hostel facility is available at CUI campuses.

question: Is hostel accommodation guaranteed?
answer: No. Hostel accommodation is allocated on a first-come, first-serve basis, subject to availability.

question: Is transport available?
answer: Yes, transport facility is available for students.

question: What is the official merit aggregate formula for CUI Wah admission?
answer:
The absolute merit formula for admission to all undergraduate programs is a weighted calculation dividing your academic history into a 10:40:50 ratio:
- Matriculation (SSC) / O-Level: 10%
- Intermediate (HSSC) / A-Level (or F.Sc Part-1 if awaiting): 40%
- NTS NAT / CUI Entry Test: 50%

Formula: Aggregate (%) = (Matric Marks / Matric Total * 10) + (Inter Marks / Inter Total * 40) + (NAT Score * 0.5)

question: Does CUI Wah accept HEC USAT, SAT, NET, or ECAT entry tests?
answer: No. CUI Wah operates under a partnership with NTS. Standard monthly NTS NAT (valid for 1 year) or the special on-campus COMSATS Institutional NAT are accepted. Entry tests from other entities like HEC USAT, NUST NET, FAST NU test, or UET ECAT are NOT accepted. International SAT scores are only accepted for international student quota/dual national seats.

question: Where do I apply for admission at COMSATS University Islamabad Wah Campus?
answer: The entire admission process is 100% online. You do not need to visit the campus to submit your form. Apply at: https://admissions.comsats.edu.pk/

question: What are the steps of the CUI online admission application form?
answer:
The CUI admission application has 12 steps to be completed in order:
1. Instructions – Read and accept the portal terms.
2. Personal Details – Enter name, CNIC/B-Form, and guardian info.
3. Address Details – Provide permanent and mailing addresses.
4. Photo Upload – Upload one passport-size photo.
5. Education Details – Provide Matric/O-Level and Intermediate/A-Level or DAE scores.
6. NTS Details – Enter your NTS NAT score (valid for 1 year from test date) or register for the on-campus institutional NAT.
7. Program Choices – Select preferred degree programs in order of priority.
8. Labour Quota – Upload documents if applying under workers children quota.
9. Other Details – Mention achievements, sports, or extra information.
10. Documents Upload – Upload scanned academic transcripts.
11. Confirm Fee – Print challan, pay in bank, upload paid challan copy.
12. Submit Application – Finalize and submit for verification.

question: What documents are required to apply for admission at CUI Wah Campus?
answer:
The following documents are required:
1. Passport-Size Photograph: 1 copy with a clear blue/white background.
2. Matric / O-Level Transcript: Matric marks sheet OR O-Level Equivalence from IBCC.
3. Intermediate Part-1 Marks Sheet: Required if applying as a result-awaited candidate.
4. A-Level Marksheet / Equivalency: O-Level equivalence or A-Level transcripts if results are declared.
5. Part-2 Roll Number Slip: Only needed if your F.Sc Part-2 complete result is still awaited.
6. NTS NAT Result Card: Must be valid (taken within one year of the application date).

question: What is the admission fee for CUI Wah and how do I pay the challan?

question: What happens after I submit my CUI admission application? What if an objection is raised?
answer:
After submitting, the CUI Wah Campus admission staff will verify your details and documents.

- If approved: Your NTS Roll Number Slip will be displayed on your portal automatically.
- If an objection is raised: You will be notified via email and on your portal dashboard. You must log in to your portal and fix the objection (e.g. re-upload correct documents, correct details) to keep your application active.

question: What are the important rules and guidelines for CUI Wah online admission?
answer:
Key guidelines for applying:
- The form submission is 100% ONLINE; no campus visit is needed.
- All steps must be completed in the correct order.
- The admission processing fee is non-refundable.
- Applications with false information will be rejected immediately.
- Candidates with a supplementary (supply) in HSSC Part-I or Part-II cannot apply.
- HSSC improvement candidates cannot apply as result-awaiting; they must use their previously declared result if it meets eligibility.
- Result-awaited A-Level candidates are evaluated on O-Level equivalence score.
- Result-awaited 3rd-year DAE candidates are assigned a flat 60% intermediate score for merit calculation.
- Intermediate (Pre-Medical) students who gave an additional Mathematics paper must apply as result-awaiting based on Part-I.
- Cambridge/Edexcel (O-Level/A-Level) applicants must produce IBCC equivalence certificate.

question: Can you give a worked example of how the CUI admission aggregate is calculated?
answer:
The official CUI aggregate formula is:
Aggregate = (Matric % × 10%) + (Intermediate % × 40%) + (NTS NAT Score × 50%)

Worked Example:
- Matric: 950 out of 1100 → 86.36% → contributes 8.636
- Intermediate: 890 out of 1100 → 80.90% → contributes 32.36
- NTS NAT Score: 78 out of 100 → contributes 39.0

Final Aggregate = 8.636 + 32.36 + 39.0 = 79.996% ≈ 80.0%

This aggregate would place you at the borderline for BSCS (80.1% cutoff in 2024). A higher NTS score is the most effective way to improve your aggregate since it carries 50% weight.

question: Is the merit cutoff lower in the Spring semester intake at CUI Wah?
answer:
Yes, generally. The Spring semester (February intake) typically attracts fewer applicants than the Fall semester (September intake), which results in a slightly lower closing merit.

For example, if BSCS closed at 80.1% in Fall 2024, the same program in Spring 2025 may close around 77%–79% depending on applicant volume.

This makes Spring intake a strategic option if your aggregate falls 1%–3% below the Fall cutoff. However, not all programs offer Spring intake — computing programs (BSCS, BSSE, BSAI) are more likely to have Spring admissions than engineering programs.

question: What are the eligibility requirements for MS and PhD programs at CUI Wah Campus?
answer:
MS (Graduate) Programs:
- Minimum 16 years of education (BS/B.Tech/BE or equivalent 4-year degree)
- Minimum CGPA of 2.0/4.0 (or 45% marks for annual system graduates)
- Valid GAT-General score (NTS) of at least 50/100 OR CUI institutional GAT
- Some programs require a subject-specific GAT (e.g. GAT-Computer for MSCS)

PhD Programs:
- Minimum 18 years of education (MS/M.Phil or equivalent)
- Minimum CGPA of 3.0/4.0 in MS
- Valid GRE or GAT-Subject score (NTS)
- Research proposal may be required
- Interview with the departmental committee is mandatory

GAT-General validity: 2 years from test date. Students can retake GAT at any time.

5. Hostel/Transport: Apply for hostel or transport separately if needed (first come, first served).

question: What is the difference between NTS NAT and NTS GAT? Which one does CUI require?
answer:
NTS NAT (National Aptitude Test):
- Required for UNDERGRADUATE (BS/BBA) admissions
- Tests English, Analytical Reasoning, and subject knowledge
- Score range: 0–100
- Valid for 1 year from the test date
- CUI uses NAT-IE (for Engineering/Computing) or NAT-IM (for Management)

NTS GAT-General:
- Required for GRADUATE (MS/MBA) admissions
- Tests Verbal, Quantitative, and Analytical skills
- Minimum passing score for CUI MS admission: 50/100
- Valid for 2 years from the test date

NTS GAT-Subject:
- Required for PhD admissions
- Subject-specific test (e.g. GAT-Computer, GAT-Engineering)

For undergrad BS programs, only NAT is required. For MS programs, GAT-General is required. For PhD, GAT-Subject is required.
source: CUI Wah Admissions Policy & NTS Pakistan

question: Is a Punjab domicile required to apply to CUI Wah Campus?
answer:
No. CUI Wah Campus is a federal university (COMSATS is under HEC federal charter), so it does NOT require a specific provincial domicile. Students from any province (Punjab, KPK, Sindh, Balochistan, AJK, GB) can apply on open merit.

However, for HEC need-based scholarships that are province-specific (e.g. FATA/Balochistan scholarships), a domicile from that region is required to qualify for that specific scholarship category.
